name: Ramp
text: We should add a high-contrast skip link at the top of every page that jumps straight to the main content, because it allows users with screen readers or limited dexterity to bypass unnecessary navigation. This is a non-negotiable option because it provides a significant improvement in usability for users with disabilities. By prioritizing this feature, we're accepting the trade-off of slightly increased development time and potential visual clutter at the top of the page. This decision aligns with our goal of making EXCAVA usable by everyone, and it's a crucial step in ensuring that our application is accessible and user-friendly.

name: Reader
text: A server-rendered skip link risks locking us into a fixed target—what if the page structure changes later and the link points to a missing or wrong element? A late-loading skip link traps keyboard users mid-tab before JavaScript runs, breaking their flow. Settle it by testing both in a real keyboard-only session with a screen reader—if either fails, drop it and use a dynamically injected skip link that updates with the DOM.
